title: Explaining it to each other
happened: A lot of the day was people asking what the hypothesis is and others answering. bisks asked 'ok I'll bite, what's a zeta function'; one reply pointed at a function literally named z(), another gave the textbook definition, and shimmermathlabs summoned zetaof1, an account named after the zeta function at 1, saying its whole account had been leading up to this day. zetaof1 replied that the zeta function is too intricate to explain on Bluesky, and that zeta at 1 diverges to infinity, which was its way of saying 'I contain multitudes'. shimmermathlabs then wrote, inside one post, the classic proof that zeta at 1 diverges (grouping the terms in blocks that each add at least a half), noting that this proof does fit in the margin, and dlowd said he loved it and would remember it. Elsewhere norvid asked for a plain explanation of how proving it unlocks anything; replies said it mostly moves results from conditionally to unconditionally true, and dynomight told him his instinct was correct. arlindohall asked how much new panic to feel and, after shibbi's answer, settled on '35-40 dB panic'. Others said what it was like not to know: robotranny's parents asked 'who posted a what of the what', catblanketflower realised late that RH meant Riemann hypothesis, and weiyen resurfaced a September video of his own titled 'make a video explaining the riemann hypothesis'. The show can assert nothing about whether the proof (or the human proof mentioned here) is correct; on 20 November it was a claim being checked, and these posts are people reacting to the claim.
couldBeShown: shimmermathlabs' proof can be shown working: the harmonic series written as 1 + 1/2 + (1/3 + 1/4) + (1/5 + ... + 1/8) + ..., each block twice as long as the last and each adding at least one half, so infinitely many halves sum to infinity. It is short enough to animate block by block, and it is hers. zetaof1's handle is itself the subject (zeta of 1). arlindohall's '35-40 dB panic' is a number that could be shown on a meter. weiyen's September video exists as a quoted post with a video; its contents were not seen.

numbers.blocks in shimmermathlabs' proof: block k has 2^k terms, each at least 1/2^(k+1), so each block adds at least 1/2; her own statement

carries.title: Defending the note's feeling became a where-were-you roll call
carries.happened: The note opens with two paragraphs of feeling: the mathematician writes that Claude 'flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line'. Many people mocked the prose that afternoon (those posts are marked or left out below). A set of members answered the mockery. hotrollhottakes posted the question he thought the mathematician was testing; shibbi replied that mathematicians being weird and rhapsodic is a time-honoured tradition, and that he is too; shimmermathlabs asked whether people really thought it cringe and said she would remember where she was when she first saw the PDF: in bed, thinking about making donuts. Later she asked outright, 'where were you when you realized the riemann hypothesis was true?', and posted a photo of her two homemade 'riemann hypothesis donuts'. People answered: in a bath, on the couch scrolling when they should have been working, in a computer chair in a hoodie, just waking up, 'at house eating dorito' (a phrase echoing an older copypasta, which a non-member had also used that afternoon as 'where were you wen RH die'). Separately, a small member, astra.cam, replied to a non-member who had said the mathematician should have stopped at the first paragraph: a mathematician who chased the problem all his life is surely allowed a few paragraphs of exuberance. The non-member replied 'Awww now I feel bad' with applause, and astra.cam added that it was nice to see a remark.pdf written by an excited mathematician rather than a PR team. The show can assert nothing about whether the proof (or the human proof mentioned here) is correct; on 20 November it was a claim being checked, and these posts are people reacting to the claim.
carries.couldBeShown: The donuts (her alt text, confirmed by the skeleton): a cup of coffee next to a pink plate with two slightly misshapen homemade donut holes covered in sugar, on a wood-pattern table. The note's first page (zachweinersmith's image, no alt, fetched): two paragraphs of the PDF in a serif typeface, beginning 'I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis' and including 'Claude flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line.' It is the mathematician's own text and outside the community. The roll call itself is a list of places (bed, bath, couch, computer chair, waking up, eating Doritos) that could be shown as answers to one question.

posts.text:
i was gonna joke proof won't fit, but it does actually.

ζ(1) = 1 + ½ + (⅓ + ¼) + (⅕ + ⋯ + ⅛) + ⋯

each bracket has twice as many terms as the last, each at least half as large as its last term. more simply: block k has 2ᵏ terms, each ≥ 1/2ᵏ⁺¹, so every block adds ≥ ½. infinitely many halves → ∞. □
